9. STAFF DISCUSSION OF SIGNIFICANT ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS
9.1 Flora
Page 9-1
Duke has already had a preconstruction botanical survey done by Dr. C. Leland Rodgers, an acknowledged authority on the subject work. Dr. Rodgers' report on the flora of the reservoir area and transmission line right-of-way are included in Exhibit W (Appendices D and G). Numbers of each rare plant species occuring in the reservoir site have already been successfully transplanted to suitable habitats outside the project area. Concerning the transmission lines, Dr. Rodgers stated that "the only plant along the route that deserves special consideration is <u>Shortia galacifola</u>." However, as noted by Dr. Rodgers, Duke's present plans for transmission line construction should leave the <u>Shortia</u> undisturbed.
Duke maintains that the results of the above studies are sufficient, and that further studies, such as along access roads, are not warranted. This is especially true since the planned routes for these roads may change prior to their construction, thus nullifying study results.
9.2 Aquatic Fauna and Water Quality
Page 9-1
Duke is presently studying the rainbow trout in Howard Creek to determine such factors as growth, reproduction, and survival of stocked fingerling. Our results show that some trout reproduction is occurring in the stream. See Exhibit W, Table 2.2-1, Amendment 1.
Duke will be utilizing such methods as sediment control, and possibly flow augmentation, to protect Howard Creek and its biota.
Page 9-2
Duke does not see a viable method to realistically mitigate the loss of the 2.3 miles of trout stream that will be inundated. This is a very minor cost to the environment considering the ast benefits of the project. However, Duke will cooperate with the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department regarding trout management plans for any of the streams on company lands.
The results of the study on the effects of Bad Creek operation in Lake Jocassee stratification have already been provided to the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department and to the FPC staff. The results on other studies will be distributed upon their completion.
